During his tenure with the Jazz, he formed a formidable duo with his teammate [John Stockton](/wiki/John_Stockton "John Stockton") and together they led the team to two [NBA Finals](/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals") appearances in [1997](/wiki/1997_NBA_Finals "1997 NBA Finals") and [1998](/wiki/1998_NBA_Finals "1998 NBA Finals"), losing both times to the [Chicago Bulls](/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls"). Malone's 36,928 career points scored rank third [all-time in NBA history](/wiki/List_of_National_Basketball_Association_career_scoring_leaders "List of National Basketball Association career scoring leaders") and he holds the records for [most free throws made](/wiki/List_of_National_Basketball_Association_career_free_throw_scoring_leaders "List of National Basketball Association career free throw scoring leaders") and attempted, in addition to being tied for the second-most first-team All-NBA selections with [Kobe Bryant](/wiki/Kobe_Bryant "Kobe Bryant") (11), both behind [LeBron James](/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James") (13).[[2]](#cite_note-3)
